Subject: Request: supplemental GPU capacity ahead of renewal

Karthik —

Quick note from our infra team: we saw another usage surge this week tied to a customer-facing model rollout. Our current Dedicated pool is hitting sustained 95% utilization during EU/US overlap windows and latency is creeping at tail. We have the renewal coming up next month (DL-2027-489) and want to avoid a repeat of last quarter.

Ask: can Redwood provision an interim supplemental capacity (flexible mix of reserved + burst) we can put into production immediately, and fold into the renewal conversation? Specifically: an additive of ~40 A100-equivalent GPUs for 3 months or an equivalent burst/reserve mix — whichever is faster to onboard.

I attached our Q2 usage export so you can see hourly tail behavior (catalyst_usage_q2.csv).

Requirements to proceed from our side:
- Quick cost estimate + SLA for the supplemental tranche
- Lead time and onboarding checklist (network/KMS/ACLs)
- A short SOW or amendment we can sign (Procurement is looped)

Happy to join a call if you want to walk through the numbers — timing is tight (we'd like something in place within 10 business days).

Thanks,
Mike Reynolds
Head of Platform Engineering
Catalyst AI

Attachment: catalyst_usage_q2.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Mike —

Thanks for the data and the clear ask. I pulled the usage file into our capacity model and tag-checked the tail behavior — definitely a tight window. We have two pragmatic paths to get you capacity quickly and protect performance during the renewal:

Option A — Short-term burst pool (fastest):
- 40 burst A100-equivalents available immediately (no long-term commit).
- Good for spikes; cost is usage-based.
- No billing commit; minimal onboarding (network and ACLs only).

Option B — Supplement + short reserve (recommended if you want price predictability):
- 30 reserved GPUs for 3–6 months + 10 burst for peak windows.
- Lower unit price for the reserved tranche; we can amortize into the renewal commit.
- Requires SOW amendment and a short provisioning window (~5 business days).

Next steps I propose:
1) Naomi (CS) and I run a quick verification call this afternoon to align networking and KV cache migration steps.
2) Vanessa / LA (commercial) provide a pricing & SLA sheet for Option A and B.
3) I'll draft an SOW amendment that covers the reserve term and fold into DL-2027-489.

I attached a quick options workbook for your review (catalyst_supplemental_options.xlsx). If Procurement is comfortable with Option B, we can prepare a DocuSign-ready SOW.

Call windows: I can join at 3:00pm PT today or 9:00am PT tomorrow. Which works for you?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: catalyst_supplemental_options.xlsx (Excel, 240KB)
